title: Lesson 13 - Data Kits: Packaging Data 360 Metadata for Deployment
description: Manage the development lifecycle with available tooling, focused on the two data kit types, what they package, and how data kits pair with packages.

questions.question: A team needs to promote new identity resolution and calculated insight configuration from a sandbox to production using change sets. Which data kit type must they use?
questions.explanation: Change sets require a DevOps data kit, which is built for sandbox to production promotion. The standard data kit is the strongest distractor and is wrong because standard kits are not supported in change set deployments.

questions.question: Which statement about data kits is correct?
options: A package can hold only one data kit
Data kits carry the records as well as the configuration
Data 360 metadata must be added to a data kit before it can be packaged
A single package must contain both Data 360 and non Data 360 metadata
questions.explanation: Data 360 metadata cannot be packaged directly: it goes into a data kit, and the data kit goes into a package. The claim that kits carry records is the strongest distractor and is wrong because kits carry definitions, not data.

questions.question: An admin deploys a DevOps data kit but it fails with an environment parity error. What is the most likely cause?
options: The kit has too few components
The user was assigned Data Cloud User instead of Data Cloud Architect
The data kit was never published
The target data space name does not match the data space used when the kit was created
questions.explanation: DevOps kits must deploy to the same data space they were created in, and a data space name mismatch triggers an environment parity failure. The unpublished-kit distractor is wrong because an unpublished kit would not reach the deploy stage at all.
